raw_evidence: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-week inspection between June 8th and 19th, judged both the impact of leaders on social work practice and the experiences of children who need help and protection to be inadequate - the watchdog's lowest grade Services for children in care were rated good, while support for care leavers requires improvement to be good Inspectors, led by His Majesty's Inspector Leanne Cooper, found that since the council's last full inspection in 2022 - when it was rated requires improvement across the board - leaders had failed to recognise and act on shortfalls in critical parts of the service The sharpest criticism was reserved for the council's "front door" - the point at which concerns about children are first reported. The match is the same while the betting menu can change with a provincial border In April 2023, Premier League clubs collectively agreed to remove gambling sponsorship from the front of matchday shirts after the 2025/26 season. The measure was voluntary and narrow. It applies to the front of the playing shirt, not to every place a betting company can appear a Sleeves can still carry commercial branding. Training wear remains available. Stadium boards and digital content weren’t swept away by the front-of-shirt agreement.
